thread_analysis.thread_summary: This is a long, repeatedly-quoted email reply chain (May 2024 - March 2025) between [COMPANY] (a keyboard manufacturer) and Allion, covering both WHQL logo certification and Bluetooth SIG certification for a pair of BLE+USB keyboards (JP and US layout models). The bulk of the thread is sales/logistics for the WHQL testing (quotes, sample shipping, USB testing, password issues, invoicing). Embedded within the later messages are several distinct Bluetooth SIG registration questions: whether a module manufacturer change under an unchanged QDID needs a registration update, whether an existing 4.2 registration can be converted to 5.0 without new testing, whether adding key codes to an already-certified keyboard requires re-application, what the SIG fee-arrival/DID email means and whether a March completion deadline is feasible, what additional Compliance Folder documents and retention rules apply, and - because the product is sold under another company's ([COMPANY]'s) brand - whose name the SIG registration login credentials should be under.
all_questions_found: Does a Bluetooth module manufacturer change (same QDID, e.g. 97470) require a registration change procedure for the referencing product?
Can an existing Bluetooth Core Specification 4.2 registration be converted to 5.0 in place without new testing, given the referenced QDIDs are already spec 5.0?

For an already Bluetooth-certified keyboard, does adding a new key code (e.g., a Mute key) to the Multimedia key ReportDescriptor require re-application, and what's the process if it results in a new model name?
Does receiving the SIG registration-fee-arrival and DID notification email mean registration is complete, and is completing registration/acceptance by end of March feasible?
What additional documents (beyond those obtained during registration) are needed for the Compliance Folder, and how long must they be retained / when must they be submitted?

For a product sold under [COMPANY]'s brand, should the Bluetooth SIG registration login (User Name/Password) be under the manufacturer's or [COMPANY]'s representative's name, and can the manufacturer ask [COMPANY] for their login credentials?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Several SIG registration mechanics were clarified: (1) component QDID changes (e.g., module manufacturer switch) are tracked at the Listing Owner/Product List level of that QDID, so referencing products need no action if the Product List is updated; (2) a registration's Core Specification version (e.g., 4.2) cannot be edited in place even if referenced component QDIDs are a newer spec (5.0) - a new registration referencing the same QDIDs at the new spec version is required, though existing test reports remain reusable so no new testing is needed; (3) HID registrations do not enumerate specific key codes, so adding keys (e.g., Mute) doesn't require re-application unless a new model name is issued, in which case 'Qualify Additional Products' is used; (4) the SIG fee-arrival/DID email signals the start (not completion) of registration work, requiring the proxy registration confirmation form; (5) Compliance Folder requirements include an operation manual's Bluetooth section, block diagram, and outline drawing, retained 1 year past end-of-sales and submitted only upon SIG audit request; (6) SIG registration ownership rules require the selling company shown on the product nameplate (here, the OEM brand owner) to hold the registration credentials, not the manufacturer.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: For each registration-mechanics question, the consultant distinguished between changes that affect the component-level QDID/Product List (handled by the component's Listing Owner, no action needed downstream) versus changes that affect the product's own registration (which may require a brand-new registration, e.g., for spec version changes, but not necessarily re-application, e.g., for HID key additions without a new model name). For ownership/naming questions, the deciding factor was the company name on the product's nameplate, per SIG certification rules, regardless of who manufactures the device. For timeline questions, past project experience with similar registration scopes was used to assess deadline feasibility.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misunderstanding QDID-level vs. product-level registration changes could lead to unnecessary re-registrations (wasting fees) or, conversely, missed required new registrations (e.g., failing to file a new 5.0 registration when needed). Misreading the fee-arrival/DID email as registration completion could delay the proxy confirmation form and jeopardize a target deadline. Failing to prepare Compliance Folder documents could leave the customer unable to respond to an SIG audit. Registering SIG login credentials under the wrong company's name (manufacturer instead of nameplate brand owner) would violate SIG rules and require correction later.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a long-running customer relationship surfaces ad-hoc Bluetooth SIG registration questions alongside unrelated WHQL/sales logistics, each question should be triaged on its own terms: (1) component-level changes (module QDID/manufacturer) are handled at the component's Listing Owner level and usually require no downstream action; (2) registration spec-version changes cannot be edited in place - a new registration referencing the same QDIDs is needed, though existing test reports are reusable; (3) HID key/report-descriptor additions don't need re-application unless a new model name is issued, in which case use 'Qualify Additional Products'; (4) the SIG fee-arrival/DID email starts, not finishes, registration - prompt the customer for the proxy registration confirmation form; (5) proactively explain Compliance Folder document requirements and retention rules (1 year post-sales, audit-only submission); and (6) for OEM/branded products, registration credentials must be under the nameplate brand owner's name per SIG rules, with credential-sharing between manufacturer and brand owner handled as a separate business matter.
